newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco produces 3.65 mln tonnes, beet, sugar cane.
newsitem.headline: Morocco produces 3.65 mln tonnes, beet, sugar cane.

text.p: Morocco produced a total sugar crop of 3.65 million tonnes, made up of some 2.75 million tonnes of beet and 0.9 million of cane in 1995/96, the Agricultural Ministry said.
The ministry said the figures were provisional.
The previous year's harvest, favoured by good weather, totalled 3.74 million tonnes, of which 2.7 million tonnes were beet and 1.04 million were sugar cane, according to central bank figures.
In 1995/96, Morocco planted 62,500 hectares of beet, of which it harvested 57,200 hectares, yielding 48 tonnes per hectare.
Sugar cane was planted in 14,300 hectares with a yield of 64 tonnes per hectare, the ministry said, but gave no comparative figures for the previous year.
In 1995, Morocco imported 477,000 tonnes of raw sugar, or nearly 50 percent of its total consumption, according to the state Office National du The et du Sucre (ONTS).
Latest official figures show that between January and end May this year, Morocco imported 246,000 tonnes of raw sugar.
COSUMAR refinery, a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group, has been Morocco's main sugar importer since sugar liberalisation earlier this year.
A stockbroker in Casablanca, where COSUMAR is located, said last month the company was expected to import up to a total of 250,000 tonnes by the end of 1996.
Morocco plans to privatise 10 sugar refineries under its privatisation programme in which a total of 114 state enterprises are to be sold off by the end of 1998.
